blueprint_topic: Management of Care — interpreting Comprehensive Stroke Center certification during referral and transfer coordination
stem: An RN is coordinating transfer of a client with acute stroke who may require advanced stroke care. The receiving hospital is Joint Commission–certified as a Comprehensive Stroke Center (CSC). How should the RN interpret this designation?

options.A: It indicates an externally reviewed advanced stroke program meeting core and stroke-specific requirements, but current receiving capability still must be confirmed for this transfer.
options.B: It confirms that the hospital can accept any stroke transfer immediately, so current bed, staffing, and procedural availability do not need separate verification.
options.C: It indicates a rehabilitation-focused stroke designation; acute complex stroke services should be confirmed at a different type of certified center.
options.D: It indicates that the hospital met stroke standards at initial review, but ongoing performance measurement is not part of maintaining the certification.

rationale: A is correct. Joint Commission classifies Comprehensive Stroke Center certification as an advanced stroke certification. Advanced certification requires the core Disease-Specific Care requirements plus additional clinically specific requirements; Joint Commission's certification framework includes standards, clinical practice guidelines, performance measurement, and successful external review. AHA/ASA describes CSC certification as the most demanding stroke certification and as designed for hospitals with specific abilities to receive and treat complex stroke cases. For an emergency transfer, CMS EMTALA guidance separately requires the receiving facility to have available space and qualified personnel and to agree to accept the transfer. Therefore, CSC certification supports selection of an advanced stroke-care resource but does not replace real-time transfer confirmation. B is incorrect because certification does not guarantee immediate acceptance or current operational capacity. C is incorrect because CSC is an advanced acute-stroke certification, whereas Stroke Rehabilitation is the basic rehabilitation-focused certification. D is incorrect because ongoing performance measurement is an explicit component of Joint Commission certification and recertification.
educational_objective: Use CSC certification as evidence of an externally reviewed advanced stroke-care program while still confirming the receiving facility's current space, qualified personnel, and acceptance before an emergency transfer.
source_organization: The Joint Commission; American Heart Association/American Stroke Association; Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
source_document_title: Stroke Certification; 2026 Stroke Certification Standards; Stroke Certifications; EMTALA Appropriate Transfer Requirements
source_version_date: Joint Commission current Stroke Certification page accessed 2026-08-20; 2026 Stroke Certification Standards released October 20, 2025; current AHA/ASA Stroke Certification page accessed 2026-08-20; CMS EMTALA transfer guidance current regulation-based requirements rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: Joint Commission Stroke Certification — Basic & Advanced Certifications: CSC is an advanced certification; any certification requires core Disease-Specific Care components of standards, clinical practice guidelines, and performance measurement, while advanced certification adds clinically specific requirements. Certification Standards: certification is awarded after successful on-site review of compliance. Performance Measurement: certified programs collect and submit standardized performance data and must meet applicable threshold criteria at initial certification and recertification. AHA/ASA Stroke Certifications — CSC is the most demanding stroke certification and is designed for hospitals with specific abilities to receive and treat complex stroke cases. CMS EMTALA guidance for 42 CFR 489.24(e)(2)(ii): for an appropriate emergency transfer, the receiving facility has available space and qualified personnel and has agreed to accept the transfer.
source_claim_supported: CSC is an advanced, externally reviewed stroke certification with core and stroke-specific requirements, evidence-based care processes, and ongoing performance measurement; emergency transfer still requires confirmation that the receiving facility has current space, qualified personnel, and acceptance.

correction_summary: Rebuilt an extremely cueable certification-definition item into an RN transfer-coordination scenario. Removed the 'only' distractor and extreme key-length cue, preserved the verified meaning of CSC certification, and separated certification-level capability from real-time receiving availability. Adversarial reread added direct CMS EMTALA support for the receiving-space/personnel/acceptance requirement, narrowed the stem to acute stroke, and accurately recorded the CMS PDF screenshot CACHE MISS.

option_audit.A: Correct; accurately interprets CSC as advanced externally reviewed capability and is directly supported by CMS for real-time emergency-transfer confirmation.
option_audit.B: Plausible credential-overreach error; incorrect because certification does not supersede receiving-space, qualified-personnel, and acceptance requirements.
option_audit.C: Plausible certification-level confusion; incorrect because CSC is advanced acute stroke certification, not the rehabilitation-focused basic category.
option_audit.D: Plausible one-time-review misconception; incorrect because performance measurement is part of certification and recertification.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All alternatives contain comparable explanatory detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four options are parallel interpretations of the same certification designation.
